requirements.text: Admit only resources covered by tenant quota and cluster capacity.
Enforce runtime isolation independently of admission and prevent noisy-neighbor budget theft.
Reclaim failed allocations and account usage once per fenced measurement interval.

problem.scope: Allocate CPU/GPU capacity with admission, runtime isolation and measured accounting as separate authorities. Compare central reservations with bounded hierarchical token leases. Millisecond units are an accounting representation, not a promise of measurement accuracy.

stages.explanation: Admit only resources covered by tenant quota and cluster capacity. reserved means one ledger transaction deducted the full resource vector from both tenant quota and cluster free capacity under a unique allocationId and fence; chargedMs counts each fenced interval identity once. [Access control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Access_control) decides whether an authenticated identity may perform a particular action. The check must apply to the actual resource and operation, including cached and asynchronous paths.
invariants: reserved means one ledger transaction deducted the full resource vector from both tenant quota and cluster free capacity under a unique allocationId and fence; chargedMs counts each fenced interval identity once.

stages.reason: Admit only resources covered by tenant quota and cluster capacity.
stages.title: Define the operation boundary

stages.explanation: Authenticate tenant and atomically reserve quota plus physical capacity. Own tenant limits, active reservations and cluster free capacity. The admission controller computes fits, but only the quota ledger owns limits, reservations and free capacity, so concurrent admissions serialize there. [Access control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Access_control) decides whether an authenticated identity may perform a particular action. The check must apply to the actual resource and operation, including cached and asynchronous paths.
invariants: The admission controller computes fits, but only the quota ledger owns limits, reservations and free capacity, so concurrent admissions serialize there.
stages.question: Which component owns the decision and its persistent or shared state?
stages.reason: Authenticate tenant and atomically reserve quota plus physical capacity. Own tenant limits, active reservations and cluster free capacity.
stages.title: Expose authority and state

stages.explanation: Queue by declared weighted-share policy with bounded per-tenant pending requests. Quota limit is not a fairness guarantee. [A queue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queue_%28abstract_data_type%29) separates accepting work from completing it. Capacity, ordering, ownership, and shutdown behavior determine what producers and consumers may safely assume about each item. Consider this case: Tenants with weights 2 and 1 queue for scarce GPUs. Capacity frees over time.
invariants: Quota limit is not a fairness guarantee.

stages.explanation: Assign one resource vector and lease epoch; reject stale allocation commands. One reservation cannot be placed twice. [Replication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Replication_%28computing%29) keeps copies of state on multiple nodes. Copying data alone does not decide which copy may accept writes or how much stale data a read may return. Consider this case: Two admissions each ask for the final free GPU.
invariants: One reservation cannot be placed twice.

stages.reason: Assign one resource vector and lease epoch; reject stale allocation commands.

stages.explanation: Install cgroup CPU/memory and supported device/network controls before starting user code. GPU scheduling isolation needs its own supported mechanism; quota alone is insufficient. [Backpressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_control_%28data%29) prevents producers from outrunning the next component indefinitely. The design must choose whether excess work waits, is rejected, or is dropped with an explicit outcome. Consider this case: An admitted job tries to use twice its memory limit.
invariants: GPU scheduling isolation needs its own supported mechanism; quota alone is insufficient.
stages.question: Can admitted work exceed its limit?
stages.reason: Install cgroup CPU/memory and supported device/network controls before starting user code.
stages.title: Runtime isolation

stages.explanation: Record monotonic intervals by allocation, fence and contiguous sequence; an exact retry charges nothing, a conflicting duplicate is rejected, and retained identities are bounded per open allocation until settlement. Wall-clock changes cannot create negative or duplicate elapsed usage. [Idempotence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idempotence) means repeating the same logical operation does not repeat its effect. Stable request identities let a retry recover an existing outcome instead of creating another change.
invariants: Wall-clock changes cannot create negative or duplicate elapsed usage.
stages.question: How are milliseconds charged?
stages.reason: Record monotonic intervals by allocation, fence and contiguous sequence; an exact retry charges nothing, a conflicting duplicate is rejected, and retained identities are bounded per open allocation until settlement.
stages.title: Usage journal

stages.explanation: Keep warm capacity under an explicit idle budget; stop only after fenced idle timeout and drain. A queued new request prevents unsafe idle teardown. [Backoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exponential_backoff) spaces repeated attempts so failures do not create a burst of extra traffic. A retry still needs a stable identity and a clear stopping condition.
invariants: A queued new request prevents unsafe idle teardown.
stages.question: What does scale-to-zero reclaim?
stages.reason: Keep warm capacity under an explicit idle budget; stop only after fenced idle timeout and drain.
stages.title: Idle pool planner

stages.explanation: Compare node leases and ledger reservations; fence the old allocation before releasing reusable capacity. Lease expiry without fencing cannot safely free capacity. [A transaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_transaction) commits related state changes together or leaves them unapplied. The database must enforce the relevant condition during the write, rather than trusting an earlier read. Consider this case: A node reports the same allocation interval twice.
invariants: Lease expiry without fencing cannot safely free capacity.

stages.reason: Compare node leases and ledger reservations; fence the old allocation before releasing reusable capacity.
